draft.title: Periods of the ancient past
card: Archaeologists name early periods by the main material people used to make tools and weapons. The order is the Stone Age, then the Bronze Age, then the Iron Age.
Bronze is a metal made by mixing copper with tin. Iron is a different metal that needs very hot fires to be worked.
These periods did not begin on the same date everywhere. A region entered the Bronze Age or Iron Age when its people began to use that material widely.
So one place could be in the Iron Age while another was still in the Stone Age. A period name tells you about tools, not a world date.
draft.remember: Ages are named after tool materials, and each one began at different times in different places.

a.q: Why do archaeologists call a period the Bronze Age?
opts: Bronze was the main material used for tools then
Bronze was the first metal ever found by people
Bronze was used by every people in the world then
Bronze was used only for making jewellery and art
a.why: Periods are named after the main material used for tools and weapons. The Bronze Age does not mean everyone used bronze at once, because different places began at different times.
a.clue: Think about what the name tells you about tools.

b.q: Archaeologists find that one region began using iron tools widely about 3,000 years ago. Another region still used only stone tools then. What does this show?
opts: Ages began at different times in different places
One of the two groups of archaeologists must be wrong
The Stone Age ended everywhere about 3,000 years ago
The Iron Age came before the Bronze Age in one region
b.why: Each period began when people in a region started using that material widely, so regions can be in different ages at the same time. The finds do not show an error, because a period name is not a world date.
b.clue: Does a period name give one date for the whole world?

a.best: Bronze was the main material used for tools then

b.best: Ages began at different times in different places
